name: Durvalumab + Tremelimumab (STRIDE; HIMALAYA)

biomarkers.note: No predictive biomarker gates the durvalumab plus tremelimumab combination in HCC. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Hepatocellular Carcinoma v2.2026, Principles of Biomarker Testing (HCC-J), molecular testing (MSI/dMMR, RET fusion, NTRK fusion) identifies subsequent-line targeted or immunotherapy options and does not select this first-line immunotherapy doublet.

lineOfTherapy: first-line systemic therapy for advanced or unresectable HCC (category 1, Preferred). For anti-CTLA4-based combinations used as subsequent-line therapy, restricted to patients not previously treated with an anti-CTLA4-based combination.

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: Child-Pugh class A. The HIMALAYA trial required BCLC stage B or C disease, Child-Pugh class A status, and no prior systemic therapy.
eligibilityCriteria.source: DeVita, Cancer PPO 12th ed., Ch. 36 Cancer of the Liver
eligibilityCriteria.locator: lines 111644 to 111648 (HIMALAYA eligibility: BCLC stage B or C, CTP class A, no prior systemic therapy)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: therapies may have limited safety data for Child-Pugh class B or C; use with extreme caution in patients with elevated bilirubin.
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (HCC-I 1 of 2), footnotes c and d; Principles of Liver Functional Assessment (HCC-E)

drugs.name: Tremelimumab

provenance.locator: line 111641 (durvalumab plus high-dose tremelimumab 300 mg compared to 75 mg); HIMALAYA context lines 111644 to 111652

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 36, line 111641. High-dose tremelimumab 300 mg is the STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab) priming dose, given as a SINGLE dose on day 1 (represented as days [1]); DeVita grounds the 300 mg high dose versus the 75 mg low dose. The number of tremelimumab administrations (single priming dose) is described in the HIMALAYA/STRIDE narrative (lines 111644 to 111652) but the per-cycle interval is not printed as a discrete dosing table in the provided sources.

drugs.name: Durvalumab

provenance.locator: lines 111636 to 111652 (MEDI4736/durvalumab plus tremelimumab; HIMALAYA). Durvalumab per-mg dose and interval are NOT printed in the provided sources.

drugs.notes: VERIFY: DeVita (lines 111636 to 111652) and Standard Guidelines (NCCN) HCC v2.2026 (HCC-I 1 of 2) establish durvalumab plus tremelimumab (STRIDE) as a category 1 preferred first-line regimen but do NOT print the durvalumab per-mg dose, unit, basis, or administration interval. The published STRIDE durvalumab dose and schedule must be VERIFY-ed against a cited source before this field is populated; not inferred here.

supportiveCare: Immune-related adverse event monitoring for both agents (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, endocrinopathies); anti-CTLA4 (tremelimumab) increases irAE frequency and severity versus PD-L1 monotherapy.
Manage immune-mediated toxicity per the NCCN Guidelines for Management of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Toxicities (HCC-I footnote f).

monitoring: Immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol as indicated) during therapy
Liver function (baseline hepatic reserve; Child-Pugh class)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold immunotherapy and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Ch. 36 Cancer of the Liver, line 111641 (high-dose tremelimumab 300 mg vs 75 mg); HIMALAYA eligibility and design lines 111644 to 111652

guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy (HCC-I 1 of 2): Durvalumab + Tremelimumab-actl listed as a category 1 first-line Preferred regimen (footnotes f, i; reference 3 Abou-Alfa, HIMALAYA). The guideline lists the regimen by name and does not print per-mg doses.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for durvalumab plus tremelimumab (STRIDE regimen; HIMALAYA trial) as first-line systemic therapy for advanced or unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (#22). The tremelimumab high-dose priming dose (300 mg IV, single dose on day 1) is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. Ch. 36 (line 111641, high-dose 300 mg vs 75 mg). The Standard Guidelines (NCCN) HCC v2.2026 Principles of Systemic Therapy (HCC-I 1 of 2) supply the category 1 preferred first-line status but print no per-mg doses. The durvalumab per-mg dose, unit, basis, and administration interval are NOT established by the provided sources and are set to VERIFY (durvalumab.dosePerUnit/basis/unit/days), as are the overall regimen cycleLengthDays and cycles; these must be VERIFY-ed against a cited source and were not inferred. Eligibility captures Child-Pugh class A per the HIMALAYA criteria (DeVita lines 111644 to 111648) and the HCC-I caution footnotes for Child-Pugh B/C. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
